intervals.label: decommissioning at Y2L, relocation, upgrade and installation at Yemilab
intervals.note: Start: COSINE-100 completed data taking in March 2023 (14 March 2023, arXiv:2409.13226). The decommissioning at Y2L was completed in October 2023 (arXiv:2409.15748) and shield installation began in January 2024 (AAPPS Bull.); first physics data September 2025.
intervals.quote: After COSINE-100 completed data taking in March 2023, the detector was upgraded to COSINE-100U and relocated to Yemilab

intervals.label: physics data taking at Yemilab
intervals.note: Room-temperature physics data (about 23 C) from September 2025; the nominal -30 C operation followed in May 2026.
intervals.quote: Stable COSINE-100U physics data taking began at Yemilab in September 2025

intervals.label: physics data taking at the nominal -30 C
intervals.quote: Physics data taking at the nominal operating temperature of −30 ◦C began in May 2026.

placements.quote: The COSINE-100U experiment is located at Yemilab in Jeongseon, Gangwon Province, Republic of Korea.

depth.quote: The laboratory is situated approximately 1,000 m underground

total_mass.quote: The detector, consisting of eight NaI(Tl) crystals with a total mass of 99.1 kg

summary.plain: COSINE-100U is the upgraded COSINE-100 experiment: the same eight sodium-iodide crystals, moved to the deeper Yemilab laboratory and re-fitted so that more of their light is collected. It aims to look for lighter dark matter and has been taking data there since September 2025.
summary.technical: Eight NaI(Tl) crystals (99.1 kg) with direct PMT coupling through silicone optical pads and 45-degree beveled crystal edges (light yield 15.8-27.7 p.e./keV), liquid-scintillator veto in a low-temperature room at about -30 C at Yemilab (the 2024 facility paper planned to reuse the copper box with about 2 tonnes of liquid scintillator and to remake the shielding) (about 1,000 m overburden, muon flux about 1e-7 /cm2/s). Physics data since September 2025 at room temperature and since May 2026 at -30 C.

technology.quote: directly couples the photomultiplier tubes (PMTs) to the crystal end faces through 2-mm-thick silicone optical pads
technology.value: Eight NaI(Tl) crystals with photomultiplier tubes coupled directly to the crystal end faces, in a liquid-scintillator veto in a -30 C room
